qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507.mistake: The main mistake is in several cases (e.g., entries 11, 14, 16), where the natural language incorrectly interprets (¬A ∨ ¬B) as "it is not the case that (A or B)", which is ¬(A ∨ B). But (¬A ∨ ¬B) is logically equivalent to ¬(A ∧ B), not ¬(A ∨ B). This confuses the meaning: the FOL expresses XOR (A or B but not both), while the NL describes a contradiction (A or B and not (A or B)), which is never true. This makes the meaning diverge significantly.
